Hi Samir / Lena,

Thanks again for the time today — good call. Recap + proposed plan below so we’re aligned on success criteria, timelines, and capacity for the POC. Please confirm or flag anything you want changed.

Call recap (what you said):
- Goal: evaluate Redwood inference for LLM-powered answers in Acme AI’s knowledge product (search-to-answer).
- Target KPIs: 99th-pctl latency target ~250ms for 512-token prompts; throughput target ~10 req/s sustained for the initial user simulation; output quality measured by F1/ROUGE on your eval set.

Proposed POC success criteria (we already discussed):
1) Latency: 99p <= 250ms for 512-token test prompts under expected load.
2) Throughput: sustain 10 req/s for 10-min windows without errors.
3) Quality: match baseline model quality on your 2k eval prompts (we’ll run same prompts).
4) Cost guardrail: estimated infra cost <= $X (we’ll provide a cost estimate).

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Feb 23: start provisioning (reserve capacity & config review).
- Mar 1: begin 2-week POC test window (Mar 1–Mar 14).
- Mar 15: review results and recommend next steps (scale/contract).

Capacity recommendation for POC (initial):
- Reserved: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline) pinned for the POC start.
- Autoscale: policy to allow burst up to 6 GPUs if CPU/GPU utilization or queue latency exceeds thresholds.
- Cache/batching: we will enable prefix caching + dynamic batching; expected 30–40% token-cost reduction.

Ownership and next steps:
- Redwood owners: Marissa (AE) - program lead; Dev Patel (Infra eng) - runtime/config; Dylan Brooks (SRE) - monitoring & alerts.
- Acme owners: Samir (product), Lena (infra).

Attachments: poc_capacity_table.xlsx (provisioning numbers + cost estimate), poc_evaluation_criteria.pdf (eval checklist).

Please reply with: (A) confirmation of POC start window (Mar 1 OK?), (B) any higher/lower burst expectations, (C) test dataset delivery ETA.

Thanks,

Thanks Samir — great questions. Answering inline and adding a few more specifics on autoscale/fallbacks below.

Warmup & autoscale behavior:
- Typical model load time: ~45–75s for a full FP16 model on A100-class hardware.
- Mitigation: we recommend burst policy that uses a warm pool (keep 1 additional idle instance in warm state) to reduce cold-starts; combined with KV/prefix caching this limits user-facing impact.
- Fallbacks: yes — Redwood supports automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant (e.g., 8-bit) if we detect sustained queueing/latency breaches. Fallbacks are policy-driven and can be enabled for the POC.

Concrete capacity plan for the POC (proposal):
- Reserved: 2x A100-equivalent (baseline, always-on).
- Warm pool: 1x kept-warm instance to cut cold-starts.
- Autoscale max: 6 GPUs (scale up in steps of 1 GPU, aggressive scale when 95th p99 queue latency > 200ms).
- Observability: 1s granularity metrics for request latency, queue time, token/sec; automatic alerts to Acme Slack + Redwood console.

POC success metrics (we will measure):
- 99p latency for 512-token prompts <= 250ms for 95% of test windows.
- Error rate < 0.5% over test window.
- Throughput: sustain 10 req/s for 10-minute windows without queue backlog.

Action items assigned:
- Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwoodinference.com): finalize autoscale policy and warm-pool config; ETA Feb 20.
- Dylan Brooks (dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com): add Acme dashboards and alerts; ETA Feb 25.
- Acme: Samir / Lena to provide eval dataset by Feb 18 and confirm Mar 1 start or propose alternate date.

I attached an updated poc_capacity_table.xlsx with the warm-pool and cost delta. Let me know if you want a quick 30-min sync this week to walk the plan.

Best,
Marissa
